source_section: How It Works - Scoring and Ranking
claim_text: Phoenix predicts probabilities across engagement/click/attention/author/negative action categories; RankingScorer computes Final Score = sum(weight_i * P(action_i)); three adjustments follow: Author Diversity (decaying per-repeat-author multiplier with a floor), Out-of-Network Discount (multiplier <1 for OON posts and for in-network replies/reposts), and New-Author Boost (lift toward a target position for low-impression authors); VMRanker then calls vm-ranker/.
notes: The weighted-sum formula, weight source (param.rs), and file/symbol existence are DIRECT. The three named adjustments (author diversity decay, OON discount, new-author boost) were not individually re-derived symbol-by-symbol in S00; deferred to S05/S08 for exact formulas/thresholds/defaults.

claim_text: Pre-Scoring Filters table lists 17 filters in order: DropDuplicatesFilter, CoreDataHydrationFilter, AgeFilter (>48h), SelfTweetFilter, OONRetweetReplyFilter, OONNsfwSimclustersFilter, RetweetDeduplicationFilter, IneligibleSubscriptionFilter, PreviouslySeenPostsFilter, PreviouslySeenPostsBackupFilter, PreviouslyServedPostsFilter, MutedKeywordFilter, AuthorSocialgraphFilter, VideoFilter, TopicIdsFilter, NewUserMinEngagementFilter, InventoryHoldoutFilter.
notes: The actual pre-scoring filter Vec in phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs contains an 18th filter, Brazil2026ElectionFilter, positioned between AuthorSocialgraphFilter and VideoFilter, that is present in the running pipeline but absent from this README table. Also, home-mixer/filters/mod.rs declares additional filter modules not in this table (ad_adjacent_served_filter, following_retweet_deduplication_filter, invalid_conversation_module_filter, push_to_home_dedup_filter, result_size_filter, self_reply_chain_filter) -- these may belong to the Blending Pipeline or post-selection stage rather than pre-scoring, which S00 did not individually re-verify. See finding S00-F002.

claim_text: Already-seen posts are handled twice: ThunderSource excludes them directly (given the list), other sources do not, so their repeats are caught by the general filters.
notes: Plausible given ThunderSource's distinct role as an in-memory source with direct access to viewer state, but S00 did not trace ThunderSource's exact filtering implementation; deferred to S01/S03.

claim_text: Post-Selection Filters: VFFilter (removes VF-drop posts), AncillaryVFFilter (removes posts whose parent/quote/repost was dropped), DedupConversationFilter (collapses conversation branches). The first VF rule that answers drop ends evaluation; a further OON-only rule subset can only drop and is listed in visibility-filtering/rules/registry.rs.
notes: All three post-selection filter files exist. registry.rs contains a TimelineHomeRecommendations SafetyLevel with its own rule Vec (timeline_home_recommendations_policy()), consistent with an OON-recommendation-only rule subset; full first-drop-wins evaluation semantics deferred to S14.

The existence of a runtime config system is DIRECT (xai_feature_switches crate in home-mixer; a full GrowthBook client/writer integration in abuse-enforcement-service). source_section: What's not in this repo? - Deployment
claim_text: phoenix/ ships a Cargo workspace, a pyproject.toml, a QUICKSTART.md, and synthetic data generation so a small model can be trained/served end-to-end; elsewhere, build/deployment files or infra imports (e.g. xai_service_runner, xai_kafka) may be omitted as 'self-explanatory'.
notes: All three named files exist at phoenix/. Whether the quickstart genuinely runs end-to-end without any additional missing dependency was not executed/verified in S00 (S00 was instructed not to spend the pass compiling systems); this is a downstream S18 reproducibility obligation.

claim_text: Under the Hood is a piloted transparency tool available at a stated x.com URL, with the jobs/serving code in under-the-hood/.
runtime_or_missing_dependency_caveat: The external product URL and its live availability cannot and should not be verified by fetching external resources in this pass (S00 is restricted to the frozen repository). Only in-repo code existence is confirmed.

claim_text: During transformer inference, candidates cannot attend to each other, only to viewer context, so a post's score does not depend on which other posts are in the batch.
notes: Attention-related source files exist and are named consistently with a ranker attention implementation, but S00 did not read the model/masking code deeply enough to independently confirm the specific 'candidates cannot attend to each other' isolation property; this is an S05/S06 model-architecture verification obligation.

claim_text: Both retrieval and ranking use multiple hash functions for embedding lookup, so there is no vocabulary to maintain and new posts are representable immediately.
notes: Files with hash/embedding-relevant names exist; S00 did not verify the specific multi-hash-function embedding-lookup mechanism at the code level. Deferred to S05/S06.

notes: Root LICENSE is the standard Apache-2.0 text (CONFIRMED). However, phoenix/NOTICE documents that files under phoenix/xrex/cutedsl/ and phoenix/xrex/pallas/ are derived from third-party BSD-3-Clause (flash-attention, NVIDIA CUTLASS) and Apache-2.0 (jax-triton) sources with their own retained in-file license notices. A blanket 'the whole repo is under one Apache-2.0 grant with no other licensing considerations' reading is therefore incomplete. See finding S00-F011.

claim_text: Future algorithm updates will be published to this repo as diffs; the bidirectional follow boost example shows what that looks like; in plain language it boosts original posts from mutual follows by increasing the weight on predicted reply probability.
notes: The checked-in mechanism (weight addition gated on mutual-follow + original-post eligibility) matches this plain-language description directly.

runtime_or_missing_dependency_caveat: No experiment-assignment log, A/B test manifest, or dated rollout record exists in the frozen snapshot. This is a historical production-operations claim that only the prose narrative asserts.
notes: The mechanism this history describes (a configurable boost value with a param-driven default) is DIRECT and consistent with the claim's plausibility, but the specific date, percentages, and value-assignment distribution are not established by source code and cannot be treated as proven from this snapshot.

claim_text: On July 13, 2026, a boost value of 20 was rolled out broadly to many users while other values (0/5/10/15) continued to be tested at varying percentages.
runtime_or_missing_dependency_caveat: The checked-in default no longer reads 20.0 (see S00-C036); this snapshot postdates the claimed July 13 state.
notes: Cannot be confirmed or contradicted from the current snapshot alone; the diff shown for this date is presented as an illustrative historical artifact, not as the current file.

claim_text: On July 24, 2026, the bidirectional follow reply boost value was changed from 20 to 15, motivated by feedback that World Cup discussion was under-surfaced because much of it came from unfollowed accounts.
runtime_or_missing_dependency_caveat: The checked-in numeric value change (20.0 -> 15.0) matches the current snapshot's default exactly (DIRECT for the value itself). The causal motivation (World Cup feedback) is an editorial/narrative claim about internal decision-making that source code cannot prove or disprove.
notes: See finding S00-F004. This is the strongest example in S00 of a documented historical claim whose end-state numeric default is independently verifiable in the current snapshot, while the process/motivation narrative around it is not.

claim_text: param.rs defines BidirectionalFollowReplyWeightBoost (f64, default shown as 20.0 in the July 13 diff) and BidirectionalFollowDwellWeightBoost (f64, default 0.0).
notes: Current checked-in default for BidirectionalFollowReplyWeightBoost is 15.0 (reflecting the doc's own later July 24 diff, not its July 13 diff). BidirectionalFollowDwellWeightBoost remains 0.0, consistent with the doc's 'not shipped more broadly' claim for the dwell variant. See finding S00-F004/F005.

claim_text: EnableBidirectionalFollowHydration (bool) is added with a checked-in default of true.
notes: Matches doc exactly; default true means the hydration mechanism itself is checked-in-enabled, separate from whether the boost magnitude is nonzero.

claim_text: BidirectionalFollowHydrator is a new hydrator that queries SocialGraphClientOps.check_followed_by for the mutual-follow status of candidate authors the viewer already follows, and sets is_mutual_follow_author on the candidate; on a social-graph client error it returns Err for all candidates in the batch.
runtime_or_missing_dependency_caveat: Downstream handling of a per-candidate Err from this hydrator (drop candidate vs. fail whole request vs. retry) is a candidate-pipeline Hydrator-trait behavior not verified in S00.
notes: See finding S00-F008. The CURRENT checked-in file (215 lines) differs materially from the diff shown in the doc: it gates on an additional EnableAllAuthorFollowHydration param (default true) that expands the author-check set beyond already-followed authors, adds a new author_follows_viewer candidate field consumed as a Phoenix model input feature (is_following_user) in candidate.rs, and adds a `!query.has_cached_posts` condition to enable(). None of this is described in the bidirectional-boost doc or the README. This is intentional/expected drift for an illustrative historical diff, but a reader should not assume the shown diff equals the current file.

claim_text: bidirectional_boost_eligible() requires the candidate to have no in_reply_to_tweet_id and no retweeted_tweet_id (i.e., original posts only) and is_mutual_follow_author == Some(true); reply_weight_for/dwell_weight_for add the respective boost only when the boost param is nonzero and the candidate is eligible.
notes: Exact match between doc's diff and the current ranking_scorer.rs implementation (function bodies are identical; only surrounding line numbers shifted due to unrelated later additions to the file).

claim_text: BidirectionalFollowHydrator is registered in home-mixer/candidate_hydrators/mod.rs and constructed/inserted into the Phoenix candidate pipeline's hydrator Vec in phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs.
notes: pub mod bidirectional_follow_hydrator; present in mod.rs; Box::new(BidirectionalFollowHydrator{...}) present in the pipeline's hydrator Vec construction.
